target.title: perf(tasks): partial sort in tasks.list to avoid O(n log n) on every poll
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tasks.list` was loading ALL task records, filtering them, then calling `.toSorted()` on 100% of the filtered results before slicing a single page. On gateways with thousands of accumulated tasks, every Control UI poll triggers a full O(n log n) sort with matching allocation pressure, causing event-loop stalls and GC jank visible as UI lag.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `.toSorted()` with a `partialSortTopK` helper that:
1. Uses quickselect (O(n) expected) to partition the array so the first K elements are the top items
2. Sorts only the first K in place (O(K log K))

Total cost: O(n + K log K) where K = cursor + limit (typically ≤ 600), instead of O(n log n) for the full sort. For large registries with 10k+ tasks the improvement is significant.

## Evidence

All existing tests pass:
- `src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.test.ts` — 14 tests
- `src/commands/tasks.test.ts` — 14 tests

The pagination semantics are preserved: the same comparator is used for both quickselect and the final window sort, so the ordering contract is identical.

## Merge Risk

Low — the sort comparator is unchanged, only *how many* elements get sorted is different. The quickselect + partial sort preserves the same ordering contract. The worst-case (K ≥ n) falls back to a regular sort.
